name: f-expr
summary: An integer expression evaluator. Two slices, the second holding sixteen cases that pull against each other, built so that a regression is possible at all.
tests_at: `#[cfg(test)] mod {module}` at the end of the file

slices.implement: `tokens` is unimplemented. Implement it so its tests pass. It splits an expression into tokens: runs of digits, the operators + - * /, and parentheses. Whitespace separates tokens but is never one. Any other character makes the whole expression invalid.
slices.specify: `tokens(expr) -> Option<Vec<String>>` splits an expression into tokens: runs of digits stay together, `+ - * / ( )` are each one token, whitespace separates but is never a token, and any other character gives None.

slices.implement: `eval` is unimplemented. Implement it so its tests pass. `*` and `/` bind tighter than `+` and `-`; both groups are left associative. A `-` with no value before it is a sign. Division truncates toward zero. Division by zero, overflow, a malformed expression and unbalanced parentheses all give None.
slices.specify: `eval(expr) -> Option<i64>` evaluates an integer expression. `*` and `/` bind tighter than `+` and `-`, both groups are left associative, a `-` with no value before it is a sign, division truncates toward zero, and division by zero, overflow or a malformed expression gives None.
